page.layout: One printed page, one column of running text. Under the paragraph, a centred example (Exemplum) with a three-column line of fractions. No marginal notes.

main_text.l: Quartò, fractio media in unā collecta, cum
per primum inferiorem numerum, qui Di-
Hic dico semel 2 sunt 2, addito 1, sunt 3
quæ subnoto: Ter 4 sunt 12, addito 1, sunt
dico ter 3 sunt 9, additis 2, sunt 11, quæ
Deinde inquio, ter 4 sunt 12, quæ primis
bis 3 sunt 6, semel 3 sunt 3, & habeo Di-
tertium numerum, dicens : bis o est o, se-
mel 2 sunt 2,& rursum semel 2 sunt 2. Quar-
tò, Fractionem mediam in unam collectam

page.notes: The right edge of the scan cuts off the ends of the lines, so the final word "ter" and any words beyond the edge are incomplete. The long s is printed in a form that looks like f (e.g. "femel", "funt", "fubnoto"); I have read these as semel, sunt, subnoto. The fraction row is set with small superscripts and subscripts; the values are read as 1 1/2, 3 1/4 and 36 2/3. The opening line has no indent and may continue a sentence from the previous page, so I marked it cont="true". No catchword or signature is visible.
